validity.recommendation: no action on existence, classification, or duplicate status -- well documented and correctly distinguished from P0219 Mojave Gas Pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION strongly confirmed, independent of any GEM/wiki material: SEC EDGAR FY2025 10-K (Berkshire Hathaway Energy Co, issuer's own current-year filing) describes Kern River as an active, FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas transmission system within the BHE Pipeline Group; USGS Open-File Report 92-447 (a 1992 federal government report, wholly independent of BHE) independently confirms the pipeline's existence, route, and 1991 construction; contemporaneous 1990-92 Oil & Gas Journal and Deseret News trade/news coverage, a current mcilvaine industry database listing, WyoHistory.org (Wyoming State Historical Society encyclopedia), and Wikipedia all independently corroborate. NOT A DUPLICATE of P0219 Mojave Gas Pipeline: the two systems share a jointly-owned 'common facilities' segment between Daggett, CA and Bakersfield, CA (confirmed by both the SEC 10-K and the USGS report), but Kern River's own exclusive mainline runs Opal, WY -> Daggett, CA while Mojave's own exclusive mainline runs Topock, AZ -> Daggett, CA (USGS: 'the Mojave Pipeline, connecting Daggett, California, and Topock, Arizona, traverses about 142 miles of the CDCA') -- distinct origins, distinct current ownership lineages (Kern River = BHE; Mojave = Kinder Morgan/El Paso lineage per prior-session research), and the shared-facilities relationship is a known, expected, non-duplicative structure, not a double-count. Two of the wiki page's 9 harvested citations could not be read despite returning HTTP 200: kernrivergas.com's About-Us/Overview and Projects/Delta-Lateral-Project pages are JS single-page-app shells (React root div only, no server-rendered content, confirmed via curl and WebFetch); berkshirehathawayenergyco.com resolves through a 302 redirect chain to a captive-portal/VPN login wall (/my.policy, /my.logout.php3). Neither was needed -- the SEC/USGS/trade-press/Wikipedia/WyoHistory chain is more than sufficient for existence, classification, and non-duplication.

The 2019 EPA partner profile ('approximately 1,700 miles') and mcilvaine's current database listing ('approximately 1,700 miles') both independently round to the same figure. Separately, Wikipedia's stub states 1,679 miles (36-inch only, 1.76 Bcf/d) -- a THIRD figure, sourced to footnotes that read as roughly 2010-2012 vintage, predating later looping/expansion projects (e.g., the 2010-11 Apex Expansion Project, which alone added ~27.6 miles of 36-inch loop) -- Wikipedia is likely simply stale, not evidence against 1,717 or 1,700. Given the current sheet value is more precise than anything found and the gap is small, staging this as a concern for review rather than an unsourced overwrite.
